content.text: {"title":"Ishika's Garden Mystery","gradeSubjectTag":"Class 5 · Science · Photosynthesis","readMinutes":2,"scenes":[{"label":"hook","text":"Ishika was helping her grandmother water the plants on their terrace one morning. She noticed the leaves shimmering in the sunlight and asked, 'Why are all these leaves green, Nani?'"},{"label":"problem","text":"Her grandmother smiled but said, 'I don't know, beta. But look—some leaves are turning yellow. Are they still alive and working?' Ishika felt worried. Were the yellow leaves sick?"},{"label":"mathMoment","text":"'The leaves are green because they contain a special pigment called chlorophyll,' Grandmother explained, pointing to the bright green leaves catching the sun. 'Chlorophyll traps sunlight and uses it to make food for the plant. The green colour is what's left over after it absorbs the red and blue colours of light. The yellow leaves you see are old—they've used up their chlorophyll and are ready to fall.'"},{"label":"wrapUp","text":"Ishika understood now. The green was not just pretty—it was the plant's kitchen! She watered each plant carefully, knowing that every green leaf was busy making food from sunlight. That evening, she drew the leaves in her notebook and felt proud of the secret life hiding in green."}],"visual":null,"equations":[],"tryTogether":{"question":"If a plant has 3 green leaves making food and 2 yellow old leaves, how many leaves altogether are on that plant?","answer":"5"},"parentPrompt":"Next time you water a plant together, ask Ishika to spot which leaves look greenest and why she thinks that leaf is healthiest."}
